description:
The DVB-T2 bit-interleaving arms of the shift and coding-permutation survey declare warm cells but skip the protocol's untimed pass over the working set before calibration, so their committed receipts misstate the cache state they measured.

## Background

Protocol version 3 (`dev/active/f547c394/protocol.md`, cache states) defines a `warm` cell as one untimed pass over the working set before calibration, and rule P-17 requires observed cache state to match the declaration. In the survey's DVB-T2 arms `dev/active/eda07788/survey/gf2-side/src/bin/gf2-dvb-t2-candidate.rs` and `xdsopl-dvb-t2-baseline.rs`, the warm branch executes only `black_box(&buffers[0])`, which touches neither the frame, the permutation tables nor the output buffers, before timing starts. The same survey's NR de-rate-matching arms run the timed operation once, as the other surveys in this epic do. The DVB-T2 v3 pilots and confirmation under `dev/bench_results/eda07788/` were measured with these arms; every DVB-T2 cell is already `not-confirmatory`, but the survey's published comparisons rest on them.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Both DVB-T2 arms perform one untimed pass of the timed operation over the working set before calibration in warm cells, and a test shows a warm request performs that pass.
- [hard] REQ-02: The existing DVB-T2 receipts stay byte-identical, and the survey report states their warm-state defect and withdraws or qualifies every conclusion that rests on them.
- [hard] REQ-03: The DVB-T2 comparison is re-measured under protocol version 3 with the repaired arms, counted in its family ledger as a further attempt, and reported with its outcomes, whatever they are.

## Notes

Measurement work runs in scheduled benchmark windows, not during working sessions.
title: Repair the DVB-T2 arms' warm pass and re-measure the interleaving family
